name: Tally
headline: The books most of Indian mid-market actually runs on.
lede: TallyPrime and Tally.ERP 9 hold the ledger for a very large share of Indian companies — including plenty with a global ERP sitting above them. AiFA reads what Tally already holds and posts back into it, without asking anyone to leave Tally.
reads: Purchase register and the daybook, as XML or Excel export
Ledger vouchers and outstanding payables by party
Vendor masters, including GSTIN and PAN held against the ledger
Stock and receipt entries where goods are tracked in Tally
writes: Purchase and journal vouchers, posted against the correct ledger
TDS and GST detail on the voucher, not as a later adjustment
The check trail against each entry, so the finding stays attached to the voucher
never: Tally stays your system of record. AiFA does not hold your books, does not become a second ledger, and does not need Tally replaced or upgraded to work.
start: An export your team already produces — a purchase register for a period is enough to run the savings check. A live connection over Tally's XML interface comes later, when you want it.
note: Tally is where the India-specific work matters most: GSTIN validity, filing status before credit, TDS section and rate, and MSME clocks all sit against the party ledger, and are exactly what generic finance AI does not model.

name: SAP
headline: Checks at entry, in the system that already holds the controls.
lede: SAP has the control framework. What it does not have is something running every control on every document at the moment it arrives, which is why the exceptions surface at the close instead.
reads: Vendor line items and open payables (FBL1N)
Goods receipts and material documents (MIGO, MB51)
Invoice verification documents (MIRO) and the vendor master
writes: Findings against the document, with the clause or rule they were tested on
Blocks and holds through the same statuses your team already works with
The audit trail, immutable and re-readable months later
never: SAP remains authoritative. AiFA does not re-post your ledger elsewhere, and there is no shadow book to reconcile.
start: Standard extracts from the reports above, for a 90-day window. Nothing needs to be built, and no basis work is required to find out whether there is money in it.
note: Three-way match tolerance in SAP is configured once and applied uniformly. Most of what leaks sits in what tolerance permits — a rate above contract inside tolerance still clears.

name: Oracle
headline: Every invoice checked, not the ones that hit a workflow rule.
lede: Oracle Fusion and E-Business Suite both route invoices well. Routing is not checking — an approval confirms someone looked, not that the rate matched the contract.
reads: Purchase orders, receipts and matching status
Supplier master, sites and payment terms
Payment batches before they are released
writes: Holds on the invoice, with the reason and evidence attached
Journal entries balanced and supported
The check history against the transaction
never: Oracle stays the system of record. AiFA reads from it and posts back to it.
start: A standard AP invoice and PO extract for the last 90 days.
note: Where a group runs Oracle at the centre and something else at the subsidiaries, the checks run the same way on both — the agents are not tied to one ERP's schema.

name: Oracle NetSuite
headline: Multi-entity, multi-currency, and the same six leaks.
lede: NetSuite handles the consolidation. It does not tell you that the rate on line four was above the contract, because it has no idea what the contract said.
reads: Vendor bills and their line detail, via saved search or export
Vendor records, terms and subsidiary assignment
writes: Findings and holds against the bill
Journal entries in the correct subsidiary and period
The audit trail behind each decision
never: NetSuite stays authoritative across every subsidiary.
start: A saved search exported for a 90-day window — the same one your team likely already runs.
note: In a multi-subsidiary group, duplicates hide across entities: the same vendor invoice booked in two subsidiaries reads as two legitimate bills to anyone looking at either one.

name: Zoho Books
headline: Small finance team, same statutory exposure.
lede: A company on Zoho Books has the same GST, TDS and MSME obligations as one on SAP, and usually a fraction of the people to meet them. That is the case for putting agents on it.
reads: Bills, expenses and their line detail
Contacts, including GSTIN and TDS configuration
writes: Findings against the bill before it is paid
Corrected tax treatment where the section or rate was wrong
The trail of what ran and what it found
never: Zoho Books holds the books. Nothing moves.
start: An export of bills for the last 90 days.
note: Smaller teams feel the MSME clock hardest — one person tracking day 45 across a few hundred vendors is a control that exists on paper only.

name: QuickBooks
headline: Bills approved on trust, checked on evidence.
lede: QuickBooks makes it easy to approve and pay. Nothing in that path opens the contract, checks the vendor's filing, or notices the same invoice arriving twice through a different route.
writes: Findings and holds against the bill
Balanced entries with support attached
An audit trail per decision
never: QuickBooks stays the system of record.
start: A bills export for a 90-day window.
note: Where a group runs QuickBooks alongside Tally or an Indian ERP, AiFA checks both the same way rather than requiring one to win.

name: Sage
headline: Controls that run per transaction, not per period.
lede: Sage closes the period reliably. The question this answers is what happened during it — every invoice checked as it arrived rather than sampled afterwards.
writes: Findings against the invoice
Journals balanced and supported, in the open period
The check trail
start: A purchase invoice extract for 90 days.
note: Multi-company Sage estates get the same benefit as any group — intercompany entries agreed by both sides before either posts.

name: Odoo
headline: Configurable enough to be inconsistent.
lede: Odoo's flexibility is its strength and the reason controls drift — the tolerance one company set is not the one another did, and neither is checked against the contract.
writes: Findings and holds against the bill
Entries posted in the open period
The audit trail behind each
never: Odoo stays the system of record.
start: A vendor bill export for the last 90 days.
note: Odoo estates are often heavily customised. The checks depend on the contract, the PO and the receipt — not on how a particular install was configured.
